top_news.title: Do Vision CIL Methods Transfer to Protein? A Diagnostic Benchmark of Frozen Protein Encoders
top_news.dek: Researchers benchmarked nine class-incremental learning (CIL) methods on frozen protein encoders to evaluate their efficacy in protein function annotation.
top_news.brief: Protein function annotation requires adapting to new labels without full retraining. This study tests vision-derived CIL techniques across five protein encoder architectures (sequence, structure, and hybrid) to determine how well they handle expanding label spaces while keeping the underlying encoders frozen.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing protein encoder architecture and CIL workflow

top_news.title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for fast on-device agents
top_news.dek: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24B-parameter model with 2B active parameters optimized for fast, on-device agentic tasks.
top_news.brief: The model features a sparse architecture that achieves 184 tokens/s on Apple M5 Max hardware. It outperforms larger models on several agentic and tool-use benchmarks, including LiveClaw and AutomationBench, while maintaining a smaller active parameter footprint for efficient local inference.
top_news.image_alt: Performance comparison chart of LFM2.5-24B-A2B vs competitors

top_news.title: Share the Symbol, Not the Vector: Training-Free Fact Communication Across Language Models
top_news.dek: SYNC is a new training-free communication protocol that allows heterogeneous language models to exchange facts using word-indexed symbols.
top_news.brief: SYNC enables multi-agent collaboration without fine-tuning or learned translators. By using a shared vocabulary of symbols to index internal states, models can communicate complementary information across different architectures, bypassing the need for vector-space alignment.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual diagram of SYNC protocol connecting two different LLMs

top_news.title: Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO
top_news.dek: Anthropic reported $16.8B in Q3 revenue, signaling a deceleration in growth as the company prepares for a November IPO.
top_news.brief: While Q3 revenue grew 45% over the previous quarter, this represents a significant slowdown from the 140% growth seen in Q2. Market analysts are adjusting valuation expectations ahead of the upcoming IPO, reflecting broader concerns about the sustainability of current AI revenue growth rates.
top_news.image_alt: Graph showing quarterly revenue growth trajectory for Anthropic

top_news.title: Introducing UL Gauntlet, a Benchmark for How Well AI Explains
top_news.dek: The UL Gauntlet benchmark evaluates AI models on their ability to provide high-quality, singular explanations based on David Deutsch's criteria.
top_news.brief: The benchmark tests 30 model configurations by requiring them to explain complex concepts, commit to a single explanation, and justify their reasoning. It aims to move beyond standard accuracy metrics to measure the depth and logical consistency of AI-generated explanations.

primary.title: Share the Symbol, Not the Vector: Training-Free Fact Communication Across Language Models
primary.summary: Multi-agent systems allow language models to solve tasks collaboratively by sharing complementary information. These systems typically communicate through text, while recent approaches also explore exchanging internal model states. However, sharing these states across architectures often requires learned translators or assumptions about model compatibility. We introduce SYNC (Symbol-Indexed Neural Communication), a word-indexed interface that connects heterogeneous models without fine-tuning or a learned translator. From descriptions only it can see, the sender selects words from a shared list and sends their indices for each object, without seeing the questions. The receiver writes the described facts into its hidden states using its own word directions, vectors fitted once from its activations. We test selective use by swapping one attribute between two objects and requiring correct answers about both changed and unchanged attributes before and after the swap, four answers in total. We choose an early write layer on four development receivers and then fix it. With three different senders and nine newer receivers from five families, four-answer success on new scenes reaches 72.0-98.3%, up to 96 percentage points above middle-layer writing, and the two largest receivers match plain text. A task-free probe predicted in advance which depths each new receiver can use (45 of 45 cases). Without retuning, messages listing every fact keep 89.6-100% success under new layouts, and sender messages reach 23.9-64.0% on a landmark task with multi-token symbols, below text but from 0% without a message. These results show that shared word indices and receiver-local directions can support selective fact use across model families without additional training.
